articles.title: Jim Cramer is ‘furious’ as Intel crashes nearly 30% — but Uncle Sam is the top shareholder. What it means for taxpayers
articles.summary: Major investors like Jim Cramer aren’t the only ones feeling the pain after a disappointing Q3 report. Every American has some Intel exposure.
articles.body:
Jim Cramer had high hopes Intel's stock (NASDAQ:INTC) would soar to a new all-time high. Now he's praying for a bounce.

In a recent post on X , the Mad Money host admitted that he's "disappointed" and "actually furious" about Intel, as the stock plunged after weaker-than-expected guidance tied to pressures on the sales of personal computers. It's now down nearly 30% in about a day, trading at $65.76 by Friday's end, compared to over $92 earlier in the week.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

Rewind to June, when Cramer went on record claiming Intel was his " new favorite stock in this market ," announcing he started buying the chipmaker for his charitable trust when it was trading above $100 per share.

Even though Cramer had reservations about jumping into a stock that already rallied over 200% on the year, he thought Intel would gain market share thanks to the AI data center buildout. As Cramer reasoned, "There's a revolution going on and this revolution requires as many CPUs as possible," referring to central processing units, the powerful processing chips used to run AI programs.

​The day after Intel's third-quarter 2026 earnings report, Cramer bemoaned the fact that company leaders didn't give investors earlier insight into their struggles, arguing "The chipmaker should have preannounced this terrible guidance."

Cramer signaled he can't justify selling his stash of Intel after such a decline. At the same time, he doesn't recommend fresh buys either, admitting he "used poor judgment because I believed in the longer-term story without thinking about the short-term story."

With shares sliding from a high of over $140 to under half that, it's understandable why Intel bulls like Cramer are fuming.

But the story of Intel's stock decline isn't just bad news for individual investors. Ever since the U.S. government got involved, every American has invested some of their tax dollars into Intel.

​In August 2025, the U.S. government became a large Intel shareholder , taking a 9.9% stake in the company. The $8.9-billion funding deal gave the U.S. 433.3 million Intel shares at an average price of $20.47 per share.​

articles.title: Intel’s stock crashes, knocking $12B from government’s stake
articles.summary: Intel is being hurt by PC sales as the AI industry gobbles memory and other components causing PC prices to rise.
articles.body:
Intel's stock suffered one of its worst days ever on Friday, crashing around 28% after the chip giant reported a weaker-than-expected outlook for the fourth quarter.

This rout reduced the value of Intel's holdings by the government by $12 billion, CNBC reports . The Trump administration had the government buy 10% stake over a year ago. Nvidia, which also took a big stake in Intel in 2025, saw its stock drop a bit on Friday as well. Much of the tech industry — especially chipmakers — were caught in the sell-off.

Intel's stock is still a profitable investment for the government so far (and for Nvidia), as it's up more than 70% for the year, even if it's dropped significantly from the sky-high prices it commanded over the summer.

The scare-off was caused when Intel warned to expect revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion in the fourth quarter when analysts were looking for around $17 billion. It also warned that its gross profit margin would decline to 37% from 43%, and it was investing so heavily, it expected no positive cash flow.

The main problem for Intel is that PC sales are being hurt by the AI industry gobbling memory and other components, and causing PC prices to rise .

"Our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on the memory prices and availability. Year-to-date system endpoint prices have increased significantly, placing additional pressure on already limited IT budgets," Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan warned on the call.

The bright side is that revenue from Intel's data center business grew 78% over the year-ago quarter. But it is hamstrung on that front until it can bring more capacity to its fabs and book more external customers for them, competing with powerhouse Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co . One of Intel's new fabs in Arizona is operational but the next one isn't expected to be online until 2028.

articles.title: Trump touted a record Venezuela oil deal. Now reality is setting in
articles.summary: HOUSTON/MARACAIBO, Venezuela, Oct 30 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump called it the biggest oil deal in history: 17 Venezuelan oilfields holding some 64 bi...
articles.body:
By Marianna Parraga, Mircely Guanipa and Mariela Nava

HOUSTON/MARACAIBO, Venezuela, Oct 30 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump called it the biggest oil deal in history: 17 Venezuelan oilfields holding some 64 billion barrels of reserves, handed to a single company.

Delivering on it falls to North American Blue Energy Partners, a little-known firm led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, who was until recently a target of US money-laundering investigations involving funds embezzled from the state-owned oil company PDVSA. The company's deal with Washington grants the US a 35%-stake in its ‌corporate parent and the right to buy 20% of output at production cost.

NABEP says it will lift oil output fourfold to more than 1 million barrels per day (bpd), up from about 224,000 bpd in mid-October.

That will be far harder than Trump and NABEP have suggested, according to ‌Reuters interviews with 15 oil workers, contractors, financiers and industry experts. Eight of them — seven oilfield workers and contractors and one business associate familiar with NABEP operations — said the company was carrying debt to contractors and struggling to hire staff and repair infrastructure.

Even the headline reserves figures Trump cites may overstate the prize.

Only about 10 billion barrels can realistically be developed within the 25-year term ​Venezuelan law allows for oil projects, Francisco Monaldi, director of the Latin America Energy Program at Rice University's Baker Institute, told Reuters. "And only if everything aligns," he said.

Terry Wade, a spokesperson for NABEP, told Reuters the company was on track. "We're at the leading edge of a Venezuelan oil industry renaissance," he said.

NABEP faces a steep set of challenges, the industry players said. The company must secure capital; compete for rigs, equipment and power plants; execute a long list of repairs to dilapidated infrastructure; and rapidly increase its workforce in a country that has seen a decades-long exodus of trained staff.

Former Venezuelan energy minister Humberto Calderon Berti told a conference in September he was convinced "the agreement will not last long," citing the company's lack of technical qualifications and short track record.

Once owned by an asphalt tycoon, NABEP entered Venezuela's energy sector in 2024 with three projects under contracts with Nicolas Maduro, the former president who was ousted by US military forces in January. It took operational control of 14 more fields ‌on October 1 under agreements with the Venezuelan government that it said included production targets.

articles.title: Chilli Beans entra com pedido de recuperação extrajudicial  | G1
articles.standfirst: Plano abrange dívidas bancárias e prevê aporte de até R$ 50 milhões para reestruturar a operação da rede, que tem cerca de 900 franquias no Brasil.
articles.summary: Plano abrange dívidas bancárias e prevê aporte de até R$ 50 milhões para reestruturar a operação da rede, que tem cerca de 900 franquias no Brasil.
articles.body:
A Chilli Beans , rede brasileira de óculos e relógios, entrou com um pedido de recuperação extrajudicial para renegociar R$ 340 milhões em dívidas bancárias.

O plano, alinhado com os principais credores da companhia, prevê novos prazos e condições de pagamento, além de um aporte de até R$ 50 milhões para financiar a reestruturação do negócio. (entenda como funciona a recuperação extrajudicial)

Segundo a empresa, as dívidas com fornecedores, funcionários e demais parceiros não estão incluídas no plano. A negociação envolve os débitos financeiros da companhia com instituições bancárias.

Itaú, Akron e Vega atuam como financiadores âncoras e coordenam a injeção dos novos recursos. De acordo com a Chilli Beans, o aporte será realizado pelos próprios credores e tem como objetivo fortalecer o processo de reestruturação iniciado nos últimos meses.

Em comunicado enviado ao g1 , o fundador e CEO da empresa, Caito Maia, afirmou que o varejo brasileiro atravessa um período desafiador.

"Passamos por um momento difícil, mas saímos ainda mais fortes e conscientes do que representamos para milhares de consumidores e centenas de parceiros", disse.

Como funciona a recuperação extrajudicial

Na recuperação extrajudicial, a empresa negocia diretamente com seus credores para tentar reorganizar as dívidas e estabelecer novas condições de pagamento. Depois de chegar a um acordo, a companhia apresenta o plano à Justiça para homologação.

O mecanismo permite que empresas renegociem seus compromissos financeiros sem passar pelo processo de recuperação judicial .

O plano pode abranger grupos específicos de credores, conforme as condições previstas na legislação.

No caso da Chilli Beans, a renegociação busca adequar a estrutura de capital da empresa à situação atual do negócio.

"Entendemos que a renegociação com credores permitirá à companhia readequar sua estrutura de capital à realidade atual do negócio, criando condições para que possa concentrar seus esforços na operação, fortalecer sua relação com franqueados e fornecedores e retomar uma trajetória de crescimento sustentável", afirmou Felipe Casotti, sócio da Akron Capital.

articles.title: Chilli Beans entra na lista de empresas em recuperação; veja casos | G1
articles.standfirst: Juros altos, crédito restrito, dívidas acumuladas e mudanças no consumo estão entre os fatores que levaram empresas de diferentes setores a buscar proteção da Justiça para reorganizar as finanças.
articles.summary: Juros altos, crédito restrito, dívidas acumuladas e mudanças no consumo estão entre os fatores que levaram empresas de diferentes setores a buscar proteção da Justiça para reorgani
articles.body:
Neste sábado (31), a rede brasileira de óculos e relógios Chilli Beans entrou com um pedido de recuperação extrajudicial para renegociar cerca de R$ 340 milhões em dívidas bancárias. A empresa é mais uma a recorrer ao mecanismo em meio a dificuldades financeiras.

O plano, alinhado com os principais credores da companhia, prevê novos prazos e condições de pagamento, além de um aporte de até R$ 50 milhões para financiar a reestruturação do negócio.

Segundo a empresa, as dívidas com fornecedores, funcionários e demais parceiros não estão incluídas no plano. A negociação envolve os débitos financeiros da companhia com instituições bancárias.

A rede de óculos, no entanto, não está sozinha na luta contra as dívidas. Recentemente, o Grupo Gennius , dono das redes Habib’s , Ragazzo e Tendall , pediu recuperação judicial, enquanto a petroquímica Braskem também protocolou pedido de recuperação extrajudicial.

Considerando todo o ano de 2026, já são 13 pedidos de recuperação judicial ou extrajudicial.

🔎 A recuperação judicial permite que empresas renegociem suas dívidas sob supervisão da Justiça. Já na recuperação extrajudicial , a companhia negocia a reorganização das dívidas diretamente com os credores. Nos dois casos, o objetivo é evitar a falência e criar condições para que a empresa continue funcionando.

Onda de recuperações judiciais no Brasil — Foto: g1

As dificuldades financeiras têm atingido empresas de diversos setores, como saúde, indústria e energia. A maior concentração de casos, no entanto, está no varejo e no consumo.

“É no varejo de bens duráveis que dói mais, e por um motivo simples: ele é atingido pelas duas pontas do negócio ao mesmo tempo", afirma André Matos, CEO da MA7 Capital.

O especialista explica que, de um lado, os varejistas enfrentam dívidas mais caras e precisam manter estoques elevados. Do outro, os consumidores dependem de parcelamentos para comprar. A combinação desses dois fatores pressiona o setor.

Para Matos, porém, os pedidos de recuperação não representam um risco sistêmico. “Esses casos foram amplamente telegrafados, com ressalva de auditor, patrimônio negativo e reestruturação anterior. Ou seja, não foram surpresa.”

Especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 avaliam que a onda de recuperações deve continuar, mas não representa, por ora, uma ameaça mais ampla a consumidores e à economia.

"Se as medidas econômicas não forem firmes, até pode haver retrocesso em pontos como qualidade de emprego e renda. Mas não vejo como um risco imediato" , aponta Júlio Moretti, CEO da NEOT, especializada em dados sobre recuperações na Justiça.

Ele estima que o cenário turbulento para as empresas deve se prolongar pelos próximos 2 ou 3 anos. “É consenso que não se trata de algo que vai durar pouco tempo”, acrescenta.

Casas Bahia, Habib's e Marabraz: as varejistas que entraram com pedido de recuperação judicial em 2026. — Foto: Divulgação

Os pedidos de recuperação judicial e extrajudicial têm algumas causas em comum. Entre as principais estão:

endividamento acumulado desde a pandemia;

Para Cristina de Mello, professora da PUC-SP, os problemas financeiros das empresas podem ter origens diferentes, ainda que alguns fatores se repitam. “A gente não pode associar a todas o mesmo problema. Tem causas comuns, sim, mas há causas muito específicas e muito particulares”, afirma.

No caso da Marabraz, por exemplo, ela cita conflitos societários e familiares que comprometeram a renovação de linhas de financiamento e dificultaram o acesso a crédito.

O cenário também é especialmente difícil para companhias do varejo porque muitas trabalham com margens estreitas. “São empresas que precisam muito de capital de giro”, diz Mello.

🔎 Capital de giro é o dinheiro que uma companhia precisa para pagar suas contas e manter as operações.

Segundo Eduardo Terra, fundador da BTR Retail, o momento em que as dívidas foram contraídas ajuda a explicar parte dos problemas. Ele afirma que diversas empresas cresceram no período pós-pandemia recorrendo a empréstimos na expectativa de recuperar os lucros de antes da Covid-19. Depois, porém, se depararam com um custo maior do que o previsto para pagar essas dívidas.

“[A taxa Selic] veio aumentando por uma série de motivos econômicos e chegou a 15%. Agora, está em um ciclo lento de baixa. O problema é que o endividamento dessas empresas, que cresceram durante a pandemia, ficou muito caro”, explica.

E não é só isso. O Grupo Gennius, do Habib's , afirmou em seu pedido de recuperação que a mudança no comportamento dos consumidores depois da quarentena foi um dos fatores responsáveis pela crise financeira. Para os restaurantes, o aumento dos pedidos por delivery e a menor circulação de pessoas nas unidades contribuíram para o fechamento de diversas lojas.

Paula Sauer, professora da FIA Business School, afirma que a rede enfrenta custos elevados com matérias-primas, energia, salários e aluguel, enquanto atua em um segmento de preços baixos e com muitas opções para o consumidor.

Relembre abaixo os casos e as empresas em dificuldades financeiras.

O Grupo Toky , dono das marcas Tok&Stok e Mobly, entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial para reorganizar cerca de R$ 1 bilhão em dívidas.

A empresa vinha enfrentando dificuldades financeiras desde a pandemia, quando fechou mais de 17 lojas, e afirmou que o cenário do setor de móveis e decoração agravou os problemas.

Valor : cerca de R$ 1 bilhão em dívidas.

Situação : o grupo afirmou que o caixa estava pressionado e pediu medidas urgentes para garantir a continuidade das operações. Mais de 2 mil funcionários tiveram os salários ameaçados pelo bloqueio de valores de vendas no cartão.

Motivos : juros altos, endividamento das famílias, crédito mais restrito, queda nas vendas e dificuldades financeiras acumuladas desde a pandemia.

O Grupo Hortus, controlador do St Marche , entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial para renegociar R$ 574,3 milhões em dívidas. A rede também acertou sua venda ao grupo chileno Cencosud, operação que depende da aprovação da Justiça e do Cade.

Situação : a rede mantém 32 lojas em São Paulo. A venda para a Cencosud foi acertada paralelamente ao pedido de recuperação.

Motivos : aumento do endividamento, juros altos, menor oferta de crédito e falta de caixa para cumprir compromissos de curto prazo. A empresa já havia tentado uma recuperação extrajudicial, suspensa em fevereiro.

Uma das maiores redes de tratamento contra o câncer do país, a Oncoclínicas entrou com pedido de recuperação extrajudicial para renegociar cerca de R$ 5,1 bilhões em dívidas financeiras. Segundo a empresa, o processo não interrompe o atendimento aos pacientes nem as atividades do dia a dia.

Situação : credores que representam cerca de 37% das dívidas incluídas no plano já haviam aderido. A empresa segue negociando com os demais.

Motivos : queda no número de procedimentos, aumento dos custos, problemas com medicamentos, dívida elevada e dificuldade para gerar caixa.

A Alliança Saúde entrou na Justiça com um plano de recuperação extrajudicial para renegociar cerca de R$ 1,1 bilhão em dívidas. A proposta prevê diferentes formas de pagamento aos credores, incluindo a conversão da maior parte da dívida em participação na empresa.

Situação : mais de 83 credores já haviam aderido ao plano, representando cerca de 54% das dívidas incluídas.

Motivos : endividamento elevado, falta de caixa, problemas na cobraça dos planos de saúde e mudança de controle da companhia.

A rede de móveis Marabraz protocolou pedido de recuperação judicial para reorganizar as finanças e renegociar cerca de R$ 140 milhões em dívidas. A empresa afirmou que as lojas continuam funcionando normalmente.

Situação : a empresa pretende preservar empregos e manter as relações com clientes, fornecedores e parceiros.

Motivos : dificuldades no varejo, ruptura na estrutura familiar que dava suporte às operações e dificuldade de acesso ao crédito.

O Grupo Casas Bahia entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial para reorganizar as finanças e renegociar cerca de R$ 17,3 bilhões em dívidas. A medida é resultado de um processo de reestruturação iniciado em 2023, que incluiu fechamento de lojas e redução de funcionários.

Situação : em agosto, a companhia demitiu cerca de 3 mil funcionários e fechou quase 300 lojas. No segundo trimestre, registrou prejuízo contábil de R$ 10,1 bilhões.

Motivos : juros elevados, crédito restrito, aumento do custo financeiro, enfraquecimento do consumo e dificuldade para concluir operações de captação de recursos.

A Braskem , uma das maiores petroquímicas do país, protocolou pedido de recuperação extrajudicial para reestruturar cerca de US$ 10,9 bilhões (R$ 56 bilhões) em dívidas. O valor chega a aproximadamente R$ 187,1 bilhões quando são incluídas dívidas entre empresas do próprio grupo.

Valor : US$ 10,9 bilhões (R$ 56 bilhões) em dívidas incluídas na recuperação; cerca de R$ 187,1 bilhões considerando também as dívidas entre empresas do grupo.

Situação : o pedido teve apoio de credores que representam 39,6% dos créditos incluídos. A empresa agora negocia para ampliar esse apoio.

Motivos : custos relacionados ao desastre geológico em Maceió e piora do mercado petroquímico global, com aumento da produção, queda dos preços e menor força do consumo.

Esse é o pedido de recuperação mais recente. Dono das marcas Habib's, Ragazzo e Tendall, o Grupo Gennius entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial para reorganizar R$ 265,2 milhões em dívidas. As lojas próprias continuam funcionando normalmente, enquanto as franquias ficaram fora do processo.

Situação : o processo reúne 178 empresas e dois produtores rurais. O grupo mantém 119 lojas próprias do Habib's, 26 do Ragazzo e seis unidades Tendall.

Motivos : efeitos da pandemia, mudanças no comportamento dos consumidores e juros altos.

articles.title: Roraima tem 17 denúncias de assédio eleitoral no trabalho após eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Trabalhadores relataram situações de coação política em apenas três dias. Ministério do Trabalho apura relatos e empresas podem sofrer punições.
articles.summary: Trabalhadores relataram situações de coação política em apenas três dias. Ministério apura relatos e empresas podem sofrer punições. Veja como denunciar.
articles.body:
Denúncias podem ser feitas pela internet. — Foto: Gil Leonardi/ImprensaMG

Trabalhadores de Roraima registraram 17 denúncias de assédio eleitoral no ambiente de trabalho em um intervalo de apenas três dias. Os dados são do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) e referem-se ao período entre a última quarta-feira (28) e esta sexta-feira (30).

Entenda 🔎: O assédio eleitoral no trabalho ocorre quando o empregador usa a posição de poder e influência econômica para constranger, ameaçar ou direcionar o voto do funcionário. O direito de escolha é livre, secreto e garantido por lei.

Em todo o país, o novo canal criado pelo governo federal recebeu 4.305 queixas no mesmo período . A região Sudeste concentra quase metade das denúncias, liderada por São Paulo (1.325). Apesar do número de registros, Roraima, Tocantins (17) e Sergipe (22) registraram os menores números do Brasil .

Os casos agora passam por análise da Auditoria Fiscal do Trabalho . Os fiscais investigam os relatos para confirmar se houve, de fato, a pressão política por parte dos patrões. O simples registro da denúncia não comprova o crime automaticamente.

Se o assédio ou a discriminação forem confirmados, a fiscalização vai multar a empresa . Além disso, o MTE repassará as informações ao Banco Central para proibir que os empregadores punidos consigam empréstimos e financiamentos públicos.

O Ministério do Trabalho também informou que estuda criar uma ferramenta para dar publicidade aos casos. A ideia, segundo o órgão, é fazer um painel de transparência parecido com a atual "lista suja" de empregadores flagrados com trabalho análogo à escravidão.

As denúncias de assédio eleitoral são totalmente sigilosas e podem ser feitas pela internet. O trabalhador que sofrer ou presenciar coação pode registrar o caso tanto no Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE), por meio deste link , como no Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT), neste link .

articles.title: FBI acusa Coreia do Norte por ataque à Binance, considerado maior roubo de criptomoedas da história | G1
articles.standfirst: Em comunicado, o FBI afirmou que hackers estão convertendo os ativos roubados e devem buscar novas etapas de lavagem de dinheiro.
articles.summary: Em comunicado, o FBI afirmou que hackers estão convertendo os ativos roubados e devem buscar novas etapas de lavagem de dinheiro.
articles.body:
Logo da Binance. — Foto: Unsplash/Kanchanara

O Departamento Federal de Investigação dos Estados Unidos (FBI) acusou neste sábado (31) a Coreia do Norte pelo ataque à Binance, maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo, que resultou no roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões).

Em comunicado, o FBI disse que o roubo foi realizado pelo TraderTraitor, um grupo de cibercriminosos patrocinados pela Coreia do Norte. A ação levou cerca de 20 minutos e tem sido apontada como o maior ataque hacker da história do setor de criptomoedas.

O FBI disse ter observado que os hackers estão convertendo os ativos roubados para criptomoedas na plataforma Ethereum, que permite realizar transações sem intermediários.

A expectativa é que eles usem serviços descentralizados e de troca instantânea de criptomoedas para dificultar o rastreamento do dinheiro e concluir a operação de lavagem de dinheiro.

O órgão solicitou que empresas do setor de criptomoedas bloqueiem as transações que envolvam os endereços usados pelos agentes do TraderTraitor para lavar os ativos roubados.

O presidente americano Donald Trump já tinha afirmado na sexta-feira (31) que os Estados Unidos investigavam a participação de hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte no ataque contra a Binance.

"Você sabe como era antigamente, quando você assinava um cheque e o sacava? Essas pessoas são diferentes. Nunca mais vemos o dinheiro. Então, sempre achei isso um pouco perigoso", afirmou.

A Binance afirmou que conseguiu já cobrir 90% do valor das perdas e que dez criptomoedas, incluindo bitcoin (BTC) e ether (ETH) estão com valores totalmente cobertos.

A empresa informou ainda que usará recursos próprios para evitar perdas para clientes e que seguirá comprando os demais ativos até repor 100% do valor roubado.

Ainda segundo a corretora, investimentos de clientes brasileiros permaneceram seguros porque são mantidos em cold wallets, conhecidas como carteiras frias. Apesar da garantia de segurança, os saques de criptomoedas chegaram a ser temporariamente suspensos.

🔎 Cold wallet , ou carteira fria, é uma forma de guardar criptomoedas que mantém as chaves necessárias para movimentá-las desconectadas da internet. Isso dificulta a ação de hackers e reduz o risco de roubos virtuais, mas não elimina completamente a possibilidade de perdas.

Em comunicado, a Binance disse que, no Brasil, segue as regras do Banco Central, que, desde fevereiro, exige a separação dos recursos dos usuários aos da corretora. A exigência, porém, não elimina o risco de ataques hackers nem garante o ressarcimento de eventuais perdas.

articles.title: ‘Hard to Know If We’re in an AI Bubble’ Jeff Bezos Says, But Should a Retiree Buy AI Stocks? — ‘I Would Usually Tell a Retiree to Buy the S&P 500’

articles.body:
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos won't call the top of the AI boom, but he knows exactly what he'd tell someone living off their savings.

Fox News host Bret Baier asked Bezos whether the industry is in a bubble. "It's hard to know," Bezos said in an interview on Oct. 7. "What I do know is the technology is real."

Good Ideas, Bad Ideas, Same Funding Round

Bezos said the trouble is that in these periods "every experiment gets funded, the good ideas and the bad ideas." He added that "in the moment, in all of the tussle of this, it's hard for investors to know the difference between the good ideas and the bad ideas."

Speculators can lose money when enthusiasm runs ahead of results, he said, but the inventions themselves don't disappear. In his view, that dynamic is "tricky for investors" and "good for society."

The numbers show why the call is hard to make. A JPMorgan Chase basket of 41 AI-linked companies has accounted for roughly 49% of the S&P 500's market value, a concentration not seen for a single theme since the railroads. Nvidia , Apple , Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon carry heavy index weights on their own.

The five largest hyperscalers are guiding toward roughly $800 billion in 2026 capital spending on AI infrastructure, while the cleanest measures of above-trend AI-related revenue remain a fraction of that. Spending is real and accelerating, but the full payoff is not yet visible.

Then Baier asked the practical question. "Would you tell a retiree to own AI stocks today?"

"I would usually tell a retiree to buy the S&P 500," Bezos said.

The S&P 500 is the broad, low-cost default that already owns the major AI companies in proportion to their size. Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Emeritus Warren Buffett and other long-term investors have given the same advice for decades, which is to own the market and skip the stock-picking contest. For a retiree, that is the simplest way to stay invested without trying to separate the good experiments from the bad ones while the tussle is still underway.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos' father fled Cuba at 16 with three shirts — then invested $245,573 in life savings to help launch Amazon
articles.summary: Miguel Bezos didn’t know what to expect when he left Cuba for the U.S. as a teen. He managed to accomplish the American dream — and helped support Amazon’s e...
articles.body:
If Miguel Bezos could have chosen, he would have stayed in Santiago de Cuba during his teens. History had other plans.

After the Cuban Revolution, Bezos's parents didn't see much of a future for Miguel under the new Fidel Castro regime. They were also concerned for their own well-being.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

​So, when they heard about Operation Pedro Pan — where the U.S. State Department and Catholic Charities of Miami brought in thousands of unaccompanied Cuban children — they saw an opportunity.

​As he recalled in a 2016 interview with the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History , Miguel "had no desire of leaving Cuba" and "never thought of coming to the United States." However, his parents saw sending Miguel to America as the way to open doors for his future.

​Miguel explained their thinking: "If you leave then we can figure out whether we can leave or not or you come back so, it was… it was a little bit of logic to it in terms of allowing them to have a little more flexibility in what options their family would have if I were able to be out of the country."

​His parents also didn't plan for the separation to last forever. As Miguel said, "This was a very temporary decision. It was just going to be for a few months or a few years and then you'll be able to come back and we'll be reunited."

​Over 60 years later, Miguel still hasn't moved back to his Cuban hometown.

​ On July 21, 1962, Miguel arrived in Miami with no English skills and only a "little suitcase" containing a jacket made by his mom and sister, three shirts, three pairs of pants and one pair of shoes. He was 16.

​From Miami, Miguel was sent with 17 other Cuban children to a Catholic high school in Wilmington, Delaware, under the care of a priest. He later moved to Washington, D.C. and eventually got his first jobs at a bank and McDonald's.

​But Miguel wanted more. So, he began searching for colleges offering scholarships to Cuban refugees and got accepted to the University of Albuquerque. Besides studying and working, Miguel added family life to his already hectic schedule. It was here that he met Jackie, who had a son from her previous marriage: Jeff.

articles.title: Wall Street's favorite stocks are in their worst slump since 2010: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Stocks with the most Buy ratings have lagged the least-loved ones for most of 2026.
articles.body:
Wall Street analysts spent 2026 piling Buy ratings onto the AI build-out. The stocks they ignored have done better.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) stocks with the biggest share of analyst Buy ratings have trailed those with the smallest share for most of the year, according to Piper Sandler chief investment strategist Michael Kantrowitz. Measured year over year, it's the third-worst stretch in Piper's data going back to 1995.

"The Sell Side's MOST favored stocks have underperformed their LEAST favored stocks for the majority of 2026," Kantrowitz wrote in a note to clients Wednesday.

This week showed what that looks like. Alphabet had its worst month in history , Intel had its worst day since 1974 , and the Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) suffered its biggest daily drop since June as Big Tech's results revived worries about AI spending.

Add it up, and the AI trade has lost about $5 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations, including about $1.6 trillion on Friday alone. Nvidia and Alphabet, two of Piper's favorites, shed about $835 billion each, roughly a third of the total.

The rest of the market has held up. The other 625 large US stocks in Yahoo Finance's count gained about $1.3 trillion over the same stretch, led by Eli Lilly ( LLY ), Walmart ( WMT ) and Exxon Mobil ( XOM ). It's the slump in Wall Street's favorites, playing out in a single month.

Piper picks both groups from the top and bottom of each of the index's 11 sectors, so this isn't tech against everything else.

Only two slumps ran deeper, in 2001-02 and 2010. Both came near big turning points in the market, the first as the tech bubble deflated and the second as stocks recovered from the financial crisis.

Why this hits more portfolios than you'd think

Most investors own Wall Street's favorites whether they picked them or not. Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) are among the biggest weights in the S&P 500, so any index fund or 401(k) that tracks it leans on their fortunes.

The slump also shows how a crowded idea can work against investors. When nearly every analyst already loves a stock, much of the good news is in the price, and there are few new buyers left to win over. A disappointment then stings.

That's what the favorites are running into. Six of the nine names on Piper's list are down this year, from Alphabet and power producer Vistra ( VST ) to Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) and Take-Two Interactive ( TTWO ). The exceptions are three AI build-out names: Nvidia, Arista Networks ( ANET ), and Comfort Systems ( FIX ).

Meanwhile, nearly all of the least-loved stocks are up, led by steady names like Kenvue ( KVUE ) and Illinois Tool Works ( ITW ). As a group, though, they've only roughly kept pace with the S&P 500. This is less about the laggards running than about the favorites falling.

articles.title: More would-be homebuyers are considering renting instead, and they're not sure they'll ever be able to buy
articles.summary: More would-be buyers are considering renting due to high mortgage rates, and renters increasingly feel shut out of homeownership entirely.
articles.body:
With mortgage rates above 7%, interest in rentals is rising among many would-be buyers.

A Zillow measure of rental demand has risen 19% from a year earlier as high home prices and elevated mortgage rates sideline prospective buyers. Both rents and typical monthly home payments are on the rise, but the cost of a mortgage and related monthly expenses have been rising much faster.

The median apartment in the US rents for $1,932, a 2.7% jump from a year earlier. But in the same period, the typical housing payment for a new homebuyer has risen 5% to $3,037.

With renting meaningfully cheaper than owning a home, many renters are feeling discouraged about their odds of ever becoming homeowners. As of this year, renters surveyed by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York put their average odds of attaining homeownership at just under 35%, down from 56% a decade ago.

Many would still prefer to own, however. The share of consumers who say they would prefer to own a home if they had the financial means has hovered between 65% and 74% for the last decade. Today, mortgage rates remain a top financial hurdle for many renters. Earlier this year, when mortgage rates were around 6.2% — lower than current levels — nearly 44% of renters said getting a mortgage would be "very difficult."

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Binance replenishes 90% of stolen crypto, says it will absorb financial losses

articles.body: Binance has replenished 90 per cent of the cryptocurrency assets stolen in a massive security breach, with the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange saying that it will absorb the financial impact of the theft rather than pass the losses on to customers.The exchange has also confirmed that 10 major cryptocurrencies are now fully backed and said it remains on track to resume withdrawals on Sunday, November 1.According to Reuters, Binance said on Saturday that the replenishment includes funds from its corporate treasury and a portion of its futures insurance fund. The exchange is also preparing to partially deploy its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) over the next 24 hours as it continues efforts to replace the remaining affected assets.The exchange said it is purchasing the outstanding stolen assets through cryptocurrency market transactions and over-the-counter (OTC) channels.Binance reiterated that customers would not bear the financial consequences of the security breach, stating that the company would absorb the losses itself."Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the exchange said.Binance said its holdings of Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Tether (USDT), BNB, Solana (SOL), USD Coin (USDC), XRP, USD1, Ripple USD (RLUSD) and Zcash (ZEC) are now fully backed at 100 per cent.The announcement is significant as the exchange seeks to assure customers that their cryptocurrency balances remain supported by sufficient assets despite the theft.Binance also announced that it had taken a fresh Proof of Reserves (PoR) snapshot at 00:00 UTC on October 31. The mechanism allows users to assess whether the exchange holds sufficient cryptocurrency reserves to cover customer balances.The latest announcement comes after Binance suffered a massive security breach on October 29, in which hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from the exchange in what analysts described as one of the largest financial thefts on record.Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the attack with high confidence to North Korean state-backed hackers, citing similarities with previous cryptocurrency thefts attributed to Pyongyang. articles.title: Prediction: A Bear Market Is Coming. Here's Warren Buffett's Best Advice to Prepare for Volatility
articles.summary: Warren Buffett earned the nickname the "Oracle of Omaha" for a reason, but his investing advice was always big-picture oriented.
articles.body:
Warren Buffett, the famous former CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA)(NYSE: BRKB), never wrote an investing book. Instead, he peppered investment wisdom into the annual reports of the company he ran, and let his thoughts slip into the interviews he conducted. What was most notable is that he didn't give specific stock advice; he provided broad guidance.

If you think there's a bear market on the way (give it enough time, and one will, with 100% certainty, eventually arrive), then these three pieces of Buffett wisdom could help you not just weather the storm, but use it to your advantage.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The Buffett quotes to live by in a bear market

Investing is not a game where the guy with the 160 IQ beats the guy with the 130 IQ. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.

The key to investing isn't to focus on being the smartest person in the room. While that may not hurt, it isn't the whole story. If you are smart, but let your emotions get ahead of you, you are likely to think short-term and make mistakes that hurt your long-term performance. That's a huge risk in a bear market, given that fear will be high on Wall Street.

Successful long-term investors have to step back, heed Buffett's advice, and remember that every bear market has eventually been followed by a bull market. And those bull markets have historically driven the market to new heights. A bear market isn't the end of the world; it is just a normal part of investing.

Our favorite holding period is forever. We are just the opposite of those who hurry to sell and book profits when companies perform well but who tenaciously hang on to businesses that disappoint.

Buffett liked to buy good companies when they traded at attractive prices. But the real magic was his willingness to hold for the long term. His goal was to benefit from a business's growth over time, which can only occur if you buy a stock and hold it. This is sage advice for a bull market or a bear market, but it is particularly important in a downturn.

What you don't want to do is sell a good business just because the market is going down. If it is a good business, it will survive and, perhaps, even thrive during the downturn. If you are being as selective as Buffett, a bear market shouldn't be enough to ruin your investment thesis on a stock.
authors: Reuben Gregg Brewer, The Motley Fool

articles.title: From restaurant guides to payments, here’s how TikTok is building a super app
articles.summary: TikTok may be working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities.
articles.body:
TikTok announced this week that it's adding an in-app restaurant guide , marking another step in the platform's expansion beyond social media. The company has also recently been spotted developing a feature that would allow users to send money over direct messages.

The social media app has steadily expanded its offerings in recent years, adding TikTok Shop, a map for local discovery, more robust search features, games, and more. It appears that TikTok is taking steps to evolve into a "super app," a single platform where users can do much more than just watch and share videos and that can actually handle a wide range of needs in one destination.

The super app model is big in China with apps like WeChat, which is kind of like Facebook, WhatsApp, Apple Pay, and an app store all rolled into a single platform. Of course, there's the question of whether a super app model would work outside of China, but that doesn't mean TikTok won't try.

Instead of switching between apps, TikTok is working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities. After taking its biggest leap with TikTok Shop, the company — which, notably, transitioned to new, primarily U.S. ownership back in January — has applied the same playbook to recent developments.

TikTok has become a popular destination for restaurant recommendations, with viral videos often driving customers to local eateries. Now, the platform is looking to make that discovery process even easier with a new feature called " Must Eat ." The community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform.

"Must Eat" draws on more than 40 million posts and comments to compile restaurant recommendations and curated lists in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and narrow their search by cuisine, price, rating, and location.

The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. It also reflects how the app is expanding its role in users' everyday decisions, from what they buy to where they choose to go out to eat.

Bloomberg reported in August that TikTok is developing a feature that would allow users to send each other money via direct messages. If rolled out, the feature would use the social media service's TikTok Pay offering, which is already available in Southeast Asia for TikTok Shop purchases.

Additionally, Reuters reported in March that TikTok had applied to Brazil's central bank for approval to operate as a financial technology company offering lending and payment services.

articles.title: 'The Fed put is very much back': Wall Street strategists weigh central bank's next move
articles.summary: Stocks have been shaky as technology takes a hit, but the Fed's latest move to hold rates steady signals that policymakers will support the markets if the go...
articles.body:
Wednesday's Fed decision this week to keep interest rates unchanged despite sticky inflation fueled by oil prices above $100 per barrel was a head-scratcher for more than one Wall Street strategist.

"In our view, the decision was puzzling," Ed Yardeni of Yardeni Research wrote last week.

"It reminds us of someone standing in a room with a fire alarm blaring and smoke pouring under the door, yet insisting on more evidence before calling the fire department," he noted, highlighting that the US economy increased at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter.

Others have questioned whether the Fed put — in which the central bank would step in to support financial markets by lowering interest rates or providing liquidity amid declining asset prices — could come into play.

"The Fed put is very much back," Darius Dale, founder of 42 Macro, said on Yahoo Finance on Thursday. Dale expects that, going forward, policy will include greater coordination between the Federal Reserve and the Treasury to influence the bond market, the government's means of issuing debt.

That coordination could include officials eventually stepping in to buy back government bonds using cash backed by the Fed, giving policymakers extra firepower to calm nervous bond markets and provide a liquidity boost next year.

That prospect helps explain why investors have continued to shift between stock market sectors rather than suffer a broader sell-off, despite concerns about inflation, interest rates, and AI jitters.

"This is a market that continues to rotate instead of go down," Dale said. "The market might be looking — eyes on the prize — at a liquidity rescue in 2027."

Indeed, most of the sell-off in recent sessions has happened in tech. Worries over AI funding and the impact of artificial intelligence on businesses such as Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) search software have left certain pockets of the AI trade reeling. Quarterly prints from Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) have put pressure on the AI trade.

Meanwhile, Healthcare ( XLV ), Financial Services ( XLF ), and Real Estate ( XLRE ) saw gains last week. Over the past month, every other sector but Technology ( XLK ) and Communications Services ( XLC ) has rallied, according to Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace data.

"Beneath the hood, the fundamentals of this AI wave still remain really robust," Stephanie Aliaga, global market strategist at JPMorgan Global Asset Management, told Yahoo Finance.

articles.body:
And you thought this week has been painful for the tech trade.

If history is any guide, the pain for tech may only be just beginning!

The S&P 500 tech sector has seen six pullbacks of 10% or more since 2023, points out Truist chief markets strategist officer (chart below), including the current one. But four of the six plunges have ranged from 14% to 27%.

"The story is no longer simply about the strength of AI demand. Wall Street is increasingly demanding evidence that heavy investment will translate into durable profits and cash flow," Lerner says.

The AI trade took a serious beating Friday, with more than $1 trillion in market value wiped away as investors fretted about weakening cash flow profiles of Big Tech as it spends aggressively on AI. The news on the cash front worsened as the weak went along.

Google showed negative free cash flow in the third quarter when it reported mid-week. That was followed by another free cash flow negative call out when Amazon reported Thursday evening.

A week ago, Meta posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012.

None of these top tech names suggested their AI spending would be slowing down, quite the contrary.

The Nasdaq 100 went onto tank 3.4% while the broader S&P 500 fell 1.8%.

The S&P 500's tech sector tumbled more than 4.2%.

"The disruption caused by AI is on full display during tech earnings and the uncertainty around which names and sectors will be the disruptors vs the disrupted," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. "This is not the time to panic and sell all the tech winners and head into the bunker…as painful as this week is the underlying signs from enterprise AI buildouts are actually more validated than a week ago…given what we heard front and center from the hyperscalers combined with last week's Meta and SpaceX ( SPCX ) numbers. That said, tech players raising money via the bond market, equity offerings, ATMs, etc. has put further pressure on the sector and adding to the overhang seen this week."

articles.title: Slate: Sneak peek and test drive of the Bezos-backed EV
articles.summary: Slate, the utilitarian EV truck maker backed by Jeff Bezos, is nearing a big moment.
articles.body:
Slate, the utilitarian EV truck maker backed by Jeff Bezos, is nearing a big moment.

The company, formed back in 2022, is on the cusp of releasing its $25,000 truck to customers by the end of this year. After years of incubation, it was a milestone for the startup, going from "stealth mode" to reveal in April of last year.

In addition, Slate aims to be cash-flow positive shortly after production, mainly because all its parts are made in America (except items like tires) and because vehicle parts are not stamped on expensive presses. The exterior parts are easier-to-make composite pieces that avoid President Trump's tariffs on steel and aluminum.

The sales pitch has brought in a number of investors, with Slate raising around $1.4 billion to date . Previous investors have included General Catalyst, Jeff Bezos and his family office, VC firm Slauson & Co ., TWG, and former Amazon ( AMZN ) executive Diego Piacentini.

With sales starting soon, Slate offered up limited drives to members of the press, so Yahoo Finance took a short drive across town.

The prototype vehicle Slate brought to our Manhattan office looked pretty much like the production version, save the camouflage wrap. The panels are a composite material that can be easily removed and replaced if damaged, and they all come in one color, a slate gray. The lights, front and rear fascia, and truck bed looked basically production-ready. The Slate has the footprint of a Ford Bronco, with a decent-size bed and even usable trunk space if buyers opt for the SUV conversion.

Inside the vehicle, the panels, dashboard, and even seat covers were still prototype spec, so it was not indicative of what the car will look and feel like for end buyers. That being said, the sightlines out of the wide front and rear windscreens were good, the charm of the hand-crank windows remained, and the simple manual side mirrors that required the user to just push the mirror with their fingers to position it were refreshingly easy (maybe more automakers should take note).

Behind the wheel, the car drove smoother than expected, which shouldn't come as a surprise given its electric drivetrain. The vehicle was well-damped and comfortable over the cracked roads and potholes of NYC.

While a higher truck suspension and deeper-sidewall tires helped on rougher roads, the overall package meant the Slate drove like a car worth double the money, with smooth acceleration and decent vehicle dynamics, given its low center of gravity. Impressive for a vehicle starting at $24,950.

articles.title: Notorious hacker says stolen crypto is like ‘holding a hot potato’
articles.summary: Ilya Lichtenstein, who was convicted for his involvement in a crypto money laundering conspiracy, says hacking an exchange can be easier than laundering the crypto.
articles.body: On Thursday, Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, saw more than $6 billion hacked from its system. Evidence pointed to North Korean hackers, who drained the accounts in a matter of minutes. But what does a hacker do with billions of dollars in stolen crypto? Perhaps no one on the planet is more qualified to discuss the hack than Ilya Lichtenstein, the notorious hacker who in 2023, alongside his wife, Heather Morgan, pleaded guilty to orchestrating a $4.5 billion money-laundering scheme linked to the 2016 hack of crypto exchange Bitfinex. In 2024, Lichtenstein was sentenced to five years in prison, but he was released early this January. He now says that he has switched sides and is working as a “white hat” hacker trying to stop cyberattacks. CNN talked with Lichtenstein about how hacking an exchange can be easier than actually laundering the crypto and how rapid AI advancements will inevitably lead to drained crypto wallets. This interview has been edited for clarity. What are your thoughts on what we do know about the specifics of the hack? This does fit the North Korean modus operandi. So, typically, they go for the weakest link. They’re not going to attack, like, Binance.com the website, because they have a lot of security there. But there might be an employee who is vulnerable to phishing who might be tricked into downloading a virus. And I think as a defender, you need to be aware of, “Where is the weakest link in the chain?” It’s not enough to just secure the front door, you have to secure all the entrances, the doors and the windows. You’ve been on both sides of this. What advice would you have for law enforcement in this case, who are trying to figure out where this money went? You may have heard that if you’re trying to investigate a murder, your best chance is in the first 48 hours. It’s kind of the same with crypto. Right now, all of these funds are moving and getting split, split, split into small pieces and shuffled around and moved together. And because AI agents can do this, it’s happening incredibly quickly. And so it’s really a race against time to just try to catch up and trace it before it grows exponentially harder to trace. At one point, you stole what amounted to billions of dollars worth of crypto. That’s what we’re seeing right now with this Binance hack. After someone hacks into an exchange and takes all this Bitcoin, what happens then? They’re probably feeling a little nervous, if I had to guess, because there are a lot of eyes on that Bitcoin. It’s all on a blockchain that is publicly visible. Anyone can investigate it. And there are very, very sophisticated blockchain analysis tools right now. And, as we’ve seen, a lot of these crypto platforms — such as Tether/USD, for example — have the ability to freeze funds. They’re not truly decentralized. And so what these hackers have to do is extremely quickly try to basically hide the trail, try to obfuscate this money. Try to mix it around, move it around. And their main goal is just to be able to move some amount of the funds quickly enough so that it doesn’t get frozen or they don’t get caught. And there are a lot of very perilous steps for them along the way of that. So, it’s kind of like they’re holding counterfeit money, and everybody knows that it’s counterfeit? They’re holding a hot potato. So, these hackers in turn will have to try to move even faster to basically somehow take this money and either exchange it for legitimate money or mix it into a pile of money where you can’t tell what’s counterfeit and what’s legitimate. It’s very tricky for them. I think they’re in a hard spot. With a crypto hack, it’s kind of two parts, right? One is actually getting into the exchange and taking the money out. Then there’s this second part of what do you actually do with the money. Which part of those is actually harder? The hardest part is after the hack because there are a lot of eyes on all of that crypto, and you have to launder it very quickly before you get caught. So you were once in this position. How did you handle the more than 100,000 Bitcoin that you hacked at one point? It’s very difficult to launder that kind of money. I know it’s hard to believe, but I wasn’t super motivated by money. I was always more interested in the technical challenge, and so I didn’t spend very much of it. And I think that that’s been reflected in court records. So, I didn’t have to fully cash out or launder a great amount of it, which I think made it easier for me. But essentially, what I did is I registered accounts at a bunch of crypto exchanges, some using my identity, some using money mules or fake identities, and then I structured it into kind of small deposits that I deposited to trickle a little bit, and I exchanged it into other cryptocurrencies. That’s called “chain hopping.” And so the goal is for anyone who’s kind of doing this kind of laundering, is all of the coins can be traced on one blockchain. If you switch it to another blockchain, that breaks up the trail. So, for example, if I have Ethereum and then I exchange it into Bitcoin or something, that’s like a separate trail, and investigators may or may not be able to link the two. And furthermore, if you kind of break this up into multiple small pieces, maybe using different identities or different exchanges, that is a lot less likely to trigger money laundering controls. I think the kind of unique, exciting and scary part of this whole thing is that now we’re in the age of AI. And so now all of this stuff can be automated at like an insane machine speed. What does it feel like to hold billions of dollars of crypto that you can’t really touch without setting off these tripwires? Terrifying. It’s terrifying, and I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone. And I think in general, like, crime is absolutely not worth it. Like, even if it seems cool, it is not worth the stress and the damage that it could do to your life and the long-ranging consequences. Once something is on the blockchain. It’s written there forever. Someone can go back years later with better technology — because the technology keeps improving — and they can trace it. And they will catch you, and that’s usually what happens. For a long time, there’s been this speculation that quantum computing might advance to a point where it could hack crypto and make it worthless. But right now, we’re seeing AI advance at this really exponential rate. Do you think AI is an existential threat to the security of crypto? Absolutely, absolutely. Because the rate of advancement of AI has been incredible. Even this past year, the security capabilities of models have grown tremendously. And so right now, there are frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic that are capable of very, very advanced hacking. But those models are kept under lock and key. There are a lot of safeguards. But then there are also open-source models that are coming out of places like China, where they’re not quite as advanced at hacking yet, but they probably are about three to six months behind. So in a few months, you can have open-source models that anyone can download that are better at hacking than the best hackers in the world. And I think potentially that’s very dangerous. Right now, it’s maybe in the hands of nation-state North Korean-type hackers. In a few months, the same hacking technology that enables something like this could be in the hands of a kid in their basement who is bored. Editor’s note: CNN reached out to North Korea’s mission at the UN for comment about the hacking allegations. Pyongyang has previously denied hacking allegations. In a statement on Saturday, Binance said it has covered “90%” of the stolen funds for customers and are “on track to resume withdrawals within the previously stated timeframe.”

articles.title: McDonald’s must face lawsuit over McRib, judge rules
articles.summary: A federal judge on Friday rejected McDonald’s request to dismiss a proposed class action accusing it of defrauding consumers about the content of its McRib sandwich.
articles.body: A federal judge on Friday rejected McDonald’s request to dismiss a proposed class action accusing it of defrauding consumers about the content of its McRib sandwich. The plaintiffs accused McDonald’s of intentionally shaping McRib patties with ridges to resemble pork ribs and make diners believe the sandwich contains rib meat, an expensive cut known for its higher fat content and rich flavor. Consumers said McDonald’s actual use of lower-grade pork products including shoulder, heart, tripe or stomach caused them to overpay for the McRib, one of its most expensive menu items. While dismissing some claims, U.S. District Judge April Perry in McDonald’s hometown of Chicago called it premature to accept the company’s argument that no reasonable consumer could expect the McRib to contain rib meat. She said McDonald’s website describes the sandwich only as containing pork, and reasonable consumers need not do research before buying a $7 fast-food sandwich. The judge also said ads highlighting the meat’s rib-like shape could support a claim of intent to defraud, though further proof was needed. “Plaintiffs’ proffered understanding of ‘McRib’ is not unreasonable or fanciful,” Perry wrote. McDonald’s has sold the McRib periodically since 1981. It contended that distinctive product names do not fool reasonable consumers, and the plaintiffs’ preference for a certain cut of pork “doesn’t turn McDonald’s truthful marketing into consumer fraud.” In a statement, McDonald’s maintained that it does not use hearts, tripe or stomach in the McRib, and has always been transparent about its ingredients. “This lawsuit distorts the facts and the claims are meritless,” it added. Thiago Coelho, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, said his clients will continue seeking accountability for deceptive marketing. Fast-food chains have faced other lawsuits over product depictions in ads and on menu boards. These include cases accusing McDonald’s, Burger King and Wendy’s of making burgers appear larger than they actually are.

articles.title: Jersey Mike's CEO says the stock is 'undervalued' after post-IPO slump
articles.summary: Late night Sub? Jersey Mike's CEO said it could be an opportunity.
articles.body:
Jersey Mike's ( JMKE ) stock has remained under pressure since its IPO earlier this year, but CEO Charlie Morrison is confident in the state of the sandwich chain.

The stock has fallen nearly 13% since it debuted on the New York Stock Exchange at $21 per share in late July. It fell to as low as $16.09 in early October and closed the month at around $18 per share.

"While the stock has been challenged, we think the shares are generally undervalued," Morrison told Yahoo Finance. He added that the chain is aiming for "long-term sustainable" growth and has posted 20 consecutive quarters of positive same-store sales growth.

In the third quarter, same-store sales rose 3%, driven by transaction growth and 9% unit growth, Jersey Mike's reported this past Wednesday.

However, the company lowered its outlook for the year, and Morrison attributed the recent softness in September and October to lower consumer sentiment amid the "spike in interest rates and spikes in fuel prices."

Morrison mentioned that Jersey Mike's $100 million share buyback program announced this past week "showcases the confidence we have in the business."

Catering and acquiring new customers seem to be the sandwich chain's focus in the near term.

"Sandwiches are very portable," Morrison said. "They're used for lunch events all the time and we think Jersey Mike's should be a leader in the catering side of the business."

Catering sales have increased roughly 17% so far this year and make up about 4% of sales, up from 3% historically.

Some Wall Street analysts agree with the push: "We remain bullish on the long-term opportunity, as we believe Jersey Mike's product is particularly well suited to the occasion," TD Cowen analyst Andrew Charles wrote in a note to investors.

Craving a sub at 12 a.m.? Jersey Mike's may be open after dark in the future.

Morrison noted that while Jersey Mike's primary customer skews older, younger customers, ages 18 to 34, make up a core part of its growing customer base.

"Our stores do close relatively early compared to most brands in the US, and as we approach this younger audience, we know that they tend to be more night owls than perhaps our typical customer base," he said.

Jersey Mike's closing times vary by franchisee and location, but most stores close around 9 p.m. or 10 p.m. Morrison, who previously served as the CEO of Wingstop ( WING ), could take a page out of the late night wing chain's playbook.

"I was with Wingstop for many years, and we were open late and knew that younger audience really, really well and knew what they're craving during that time frame," Morrison said. "I don't think alcohol needs to play into it to be successful, but I do think there is a real opportunity to still share of those occasions over time."

Jersey Mike's plans to test that approach for now before making any changes to its hours.

articles.title: Indigenous bullet train B28 undergoes 'squeeze test'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Delhi: The country’s first indigenous high-speed train, B28, has undergone the vehicle body shell test, also known as the “squeeze test”,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Delhi: The country’s first indigenous high-speed train, B28, has undergone the vehicle body shell test, also known as the “squeeze test”, an important safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure in case of a collision or crash.The test was conducted at BEML’s production facility in Bengaluru. The central PSU is manufacturing the first two of indigenous bullet trains, each comprising eight coaches. The trains have been designed for an operating speed of 249 kmph and a testing speed of 275 kmph, as per a BEML tender document.People aware of the development said the squeeze test is crucial as the trains will operate at high speeds and their car bodies must be capable of withstanding heavy forces in the event of a collision or accident.“After the successful completion of this test, the prototype should ideally be ready in less than six months. Since the B28 (Bharat 28) train is not being built on Japanese Shinkansen technology, the development process should not take much time. The squeeze test establishes whether the body retains its shape under pressure and whether the passenger compartment maintains its structural integrity,” an official said.The railways plans to begin trial runs of B28 on the 100-km Surat-Vapi section of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed Rail corridor by May-June 2027. Commercial operations on this stretch are scheduled to begin in August 2027.While seeking Cabinet approval for the escalated cost of the country’s first bullet train project, the railway ministry had stated that two prototype trains were expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. It had also said that the entire Gujarat section of the corridor was expected to be completed by December 2027, while the full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by December 2030.You use AI every day. articles.title: ACA open enrollment: Premium hikes and what else to expect for 2027
articles.summary: The window to sign up for 2027 healthcare coverage under the Affordable Care Act opens Sunday in most states.  Here's what you need to know.
articles.body:
The window to sign up for 2027 healthcare coverage under the Affordable Care Act opens Sunday in most states.

With healthcare costs a top concern for Americans already slammed by sticky inflation, this year's enrollment — running through Dec. 15 to get a plan that starts Jan. 1 — comes at a time when monthly premiums are climbing and insurers are shutting plans.

For 2027, average full-price premiums on federal and state-run marketplace plans are set to increase by roughly 13%, according to a new KFF analysis published on Friday. Most price hikes across the country range from 10% to 20%.

States that run their own enrollment platforms are seeing premium increases of 16%, per the researchers.

The increases are being driven by a rise in overall medical care costs, inflation, and labor shortages.

"Automatically renewing your current coverage before looking at alternatives is a big mistake," Louise Norris, a health policy analyst for healthinsurance.org, told Yahoo Finance.

This will be the second year in a row of double-digit increases. For many people, 2026 ACA premiums jumped more than 20% and higher earners lost premium subsidies entirely.

Premium hikes vary widely from state to state. In Vermont, for example, there is likely to be an average increase of 3% compared to an average hike of almost 28% in Arizona.

In about half the states, the plans available are from the same insurance companies in 2027 as they were in 2026.

But those plans could be changing in terms of what they cover, what providers are in the network, what drugs are covered, the deductible amount, and the out-of-pocket maximum. Those are the sorts of things that change every year, Norris said.

And there are quite a few folks whose 2026 plan is not available for renewal next year. In 26 states, at least one insurer is leaving the marketplace.

"If it's your plan, it's a big issue to you," she added.

As of this past week, 11 carriers have announced that they will exit the ACA marketplaces, either in some or all states. Cigna, which has more than 350,000 ACA enrollees, will exit all 11 states where it offers ACA plans.

"We did not make this decision lightly and appreciate the importance of ensuring patients have continuity through the transition, and we will support members through their open enrollment transitions into 2027," Brian Evanko, Cigna Group's president and CEO, said in an earnings call. "This is a small business for us today, and it's been shrinking in recent years."

articles.title: AAIB for better coordination between civil, defence aviation authorities
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has sought a greater collaboration between civil aviation and defence authorities as a number
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has sought a greater collaboration between civil aviation and defence authorities as a number of airports where commercial flights operate are defence airfields. Submitting its final report in a case at the Navy’s Dabolim Airport in Goa where an Air India Express flight and a Naval aircraft had ended up on the same runway at the same time, the AAIB has sought the establishment of “a formal framework for collaboration between DGCA/AAIB and defence on a priority basis” to ensure exchange of unclassified information and evidence for investigation of an incident or accident.On April 3, 2026, a scheduled flight of AI Express was to take off from Dabolim for Delhi. Due to misunderstanding and miscommunication between the flight deck and ATC, it entered an active runway when a Naval “fighter was rolling” and the incident was a “near miss”. “On seeing the Navy aircraft at lift off, in the opposite direction the pilot-in-command of AI Express 1109 mentioned to the trainee first officer that the fighter did a low pass, as per the cockpit flight recorder recording,” says the report.In its safety recommendations, AAIB has asked the Airports Authority of India (AAI) “to issue a circular to sensitise air traffic controllers for emphasising the use of standard phraseology and to review the use of phrases like ‘expect backtrack’ by ground controllers which can be easily misinterpreted as ‘enter backtrack’. ATCOs must listen carefully to the read-back and correct any factual error or any apparent misunderstanding.”The investigator has asked a taxiway of Dabolim airport to be “considered as a hotspot due to its proximity with bays of civil apron and increased probability of the risk of potential ground collisions and runway incursions.”The Navy has been advised to “publish installation of stop bars and their usage at Dabolim airport (and it may) consider establishing a standard frequency change over procedure for civil traffic transitioning from the ground frequency to the tower frequency, in order to avoid recurring confusion regarding the appropriate frequency to be used.”The crew of the AI Express flight has been asked to “undergo counselling and pilot-in-command to undergo training on the safety lapses that resulted in the runway incursion due to lack of operational clarity and communication miss outs.” The airline has to issue a circular to “sensitise all crew for the lapses encountered in this occurrence.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Dream's series-extending Game 6 win was fifth most-watched WNBA Finals game ever despite early tip
articles.summary: Even with a 12:30 p.m. ET start, the latest showdown between Atlanta and Golden State drew strong viewership numbers.
articles.body:
The scheduling complications leading up to Game 6 of this year's WNBA Finals fueled plenty of contentious conversation . Ultimately, however, the much-discussed and controversial 12:30 p.m. ET start didn't affect the attendance at Atlanta's State Farm Arena on Thursday afternoon.

The Dream announced a sellout, and the crowd's energy was palpable throughout the home team's series-extending 80-69 victory over the Golden State Valkyries .

Plus, according to a Saturday release from USA Sports PR, Game 6 was the fifth most-watched WNBA Finals game on cable to date.

USA Sports' coverage averaged 1.5 million viewers across linear platforms — USA Network, E! and SYFY — and streaming, which was led by Peacock. That figure, based on Nielsen panel-only data and digital data from Adobe Analytics, represents a 4% increase in viewership from last year's WNBA Finals series-clinching game, which the Las Vegas Aces won 97-86 to sweep the Phoenix Mercury. Granted, the Aces came into that matchup with a 3-0 series lead, but it tipped off in prime time at 8 p.m. ET on a Friday.

It's also worth noting that, when factoring in encore presentations on USA Network and CNBC in the original 8 p.m. ET broadcast window on Thursday, USA Sports averaged a total of 1.7 million viewers for this year's Game 6.

That signified the second time USA Sports has averaged that many viewers for a rescheduled WNBA Finals game, after the third game in the series was the most-watched WNBA Finals Game 3 since 1999 , following its move from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21.

Heading into the series, the location of the Dream's home games was undecided. The team's arena, the Gateway Center Arena at College Park, holds just 3,500 fans. Atlanta had been hosting its playoff games at State Farm Arena, which seats north of 17,000 people, but is also where the NBA's Hawks play.

In order to keep playing at State Farm Arena, the Dream and the W had to work with the Hawks' regular-season schedule, leading to a particularly large headache during the heart of the WNBA Finals.

If the stadium was going to fit both a previously scheduled Hawks game on Thursday night, as well as Game 6 of the WNBA Finals that same day, Game 6 was going to have to tip off early, a highly scrutinized compromise.

Dream ownership clarified this week that, months ago, and again during the playoffs, it raised concerns about scheduling conflicts like that one . Those concerns, according to Dream ownership, "did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

There ended up not being a rushed championship celebration Thursday afternoon, as the Valkyries — then up 3-2 in the series — were defeated by an Atlanta squad that came out firing from beyond the arc.

Even though the Dream finished the first quarter with a 17-point lead and went up by as many as 25 points, Golden State rallied to make things interesting late. Watch parties — including those in the West, where it was still morning at the time of tipoff — were popping with fervor .

Up next is the first-ever WNBA Finals Game 7. Whoever wins will take home their first league title in franchise history.

The winner-take-all contest is taking place Saturday night at 8 p.m. ET in San Francisco's Chase Center.
